title: Fundamental flag sections cut out the individual Bruhat boundary components
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and with every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial; finite central means a finite group scheme commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ (a maximal subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^d$) and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ (a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup). Use the positive roots in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\}$, character lattice $X^*(T)$, unipotent radical $U$, and projection $p:B\to T$ of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $\omega_i\in X^*(T)$ be the fundamental characters with $\langle\omega_i,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle=\delta_{ij}$ [lem-sfb-simply-connected-character-lattice]. Put $Q=S/B$, let $n_0$ represent the Weyl element carrying the positive roots to the negative roots, and let $C\subseteq Q$ be the open image of $U\to Q$, $u\mapsto un_0B$, of [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts]. Put $M_{\omega_i}=\mathcal L_{-\omega_i\circ p}$ [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], associated to $(g,z)\cdot b=(gb,\omega_i(p(b))z)$. There exist nonzero sections $s_i\in\Gamma(Q,M_{\omega_i})$ for $1\leq i\leq r$ whose zero loci $Z(s_i)=\{x\in Q:s_i(x)=0\text{ in }M_{\omega_i}\otimes\kappa(x)\}$ are pairwise distinct irreducible closed subsets and are exactly the irreducible components of $Q\setminus C$. In particular $Q\setminus C=\bigcup_{i=1}^rZ(s_i)$. No matching between the indices $i$ and a specified ordering of the Schubert boundary components is asserted. The statement holds in every characteristic; if $S$ is trivial, $r=0$ and the boundary and the family of sections are empty.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-opposite-schubert-picard-basis] to $G=S$. It gives opposite divisors $E_i$, curves $R_j$, the injective degree map $d:\operatorname{Pic}(Q)\to\mathbf Z^r$, and the distinct boundary components $|D_i|$ with $D_i=n_0E_i$. In particular $d([\mathcal O_Q(E_i)])=(\delta_{ij})_j$. This input is geometric and does not identify any homogeneous line bundle.

source.place: Brion--Kumar, section 2.1 (6), Exercise 2.2.E(2), pp.63,70--71; local PDF WANTED, read online

proof.text: The fundamental characters are actual characters and satisfy $\langle\omega_i,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle=\delta_{ij}$ by [lem-sfb-simply-connected-character-lattice]. Apply [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-schubert-curve-degree] with $\lambda=\omega_i$ and the action $(g,z)b=(gb,\omega_i(p(b))z)$ specified in the statement. Thus $d([M_{\omega_i}])=(\delta_{ij})_j=d([\mathcal O_Q(E_i)])$. Injectivity of $d$ from [lem-sfb-opposite-schubert-picard-basis] gives an isomorphism $\phi_i:\mathcal O_Q(E_i)\xrightarrow\sim M_{\omega_i}$ for each $i$. Equality of Picard classes here means existence of an isomorphism of invertible sheaves.

source.place: Milne Remark 22.49, p.480; Brion--Kumar Exercises 2.2.E(2)--(3), pp.70--71; local PDF WANTED, read online

proof.text: Construct $t_i\in\Gamma(Q,\mathcal O_Q(E_i))$ as the inclusion $\mathcal I_{E_i}\to\mathcal O_Q$ in its dual [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Locally if $\mathcal I_{E_i}=(f)$, the dual has frame $e$ with $e(f)=1$ and $t_i=fe$; hence $t_i(x)=0$ in the residue-field fibre exactly when $f\in\mathfrak m_x$, namely $x\in|E_i|$. The homogeneous line bundle has its left $S$-action [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], since left multiplication on $g$ commutes with the right $B$-action. Define $s_i(x)=n_0\cdot\phi_i(t_i(n_0^{-1}x))$. Both the line-bundle isomorphism and the action induce fibre isomorphisms, so $s_i(x)=0$ exactly when $n_0^{-1}x\in|E_i|$. Therefore $Z(s_i)=|D_i|$.

source.place: Stacks Tags 01WX (definition-invertible-sheaf-effective-Cartier-divisor), 01X0 (lemma-characterize-OD); explicit local calculation and homogeneous translation

proof.text: By step 1 the sets $|D_i|$ are precisely the pairwise distinct irreducible boundary components. Each $s_i$ is nonzero: its fibre is nonzero at every point of the nonempty open cell $C$, which is disjoint from all $|D_i|$. Thus their zero loci have all the asserted properties and their union is $Q\setminus C$. When $S$ is trivial, $r=0$; step 1 already gives empty boundary, so the empty choice of sections proves the assertion.
